messages:
maya: FYI CI flagged a regression on INT8 serving perf this morning, looks like p50 latency up ~28% on short-chat workload. rolling dashboard: https://redwood.example/dash/serving/int8-canary :thinking_face:
ci-bot: PERF CHECK: job=canary-int8 #build 4821 -> p50=34ms (baseline 26ms), p95=98ms (baseline 72ms). regression: +30% p50, +36% p95. testset=short-chat-1k, runs=10
ajay: ugh. any recent merges touching kernel selection or batching?
maya: suspecting two changes: PR #4152 (kernel routing heuristics) and PR #4187 (kv-cache access order tweak). both merged in the window.
sam: quick bisect: started from canary head, narrowed to range -> git bisect points to commit abcdef1 (merge PR 4152) as first bad. numbers attached.
laura: interestingly, profiles show extra dequant on the hotpath when kv cache hits are >60%: we see dequant ops executed per token increase from 0.8 to 1.6 on average. that doubles the dequant overhead and blows up latency on short requests.
perf-bot: flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/fg/1795012345/ -- top stack shows kernel_selector::choose_path -> dequant::apply -> runtime::dispatch_dequant
ajay: can you paste the perf stat snippet?
laura: here: ```# perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-misses -r 5 ./serve_canary --profile short-chat
Run 1: cycles 1.2e9, instructions 6.3e8, cache-misses 12k
Run 5: cycles 1.18e9, instructions 6.25e8, cache-misses 11.8k
avg p50 latency: 34ms
```
maya: note kernel routing now prefers the "fallback-int8-dequant-safe" path for sequence len < 32 if kv-cache hit ratio > 50%. That fallback forces a slow dequant path for many small chats. PR description said slightly safer numerics, but cost seems high.
ajay: hmm we added extra heuristic to avoid precision jitter. maybe the threshold was too low. can we try flipping the condition locally?
sam: quick experiment: patched selector to require kv-cache hit > 80% before fallback -> p50 back to 26ms on the same run. so threshold tuning fixes it.
laura: but also noticed batching heuristics interact: the fallback path disables continuous batching for a microsecond window because it marks request "non-batchable" while switching kernels. that reduces effective batch size from 8->3 for many requests. combo effect = big perf hit.
maya: plan: 1) hold the canary rollout, 2) revert PR 4152 on canary branch, 3) open follow-up to (a) raise kv-cache threshold and (b) avoid toggling batchability on kernel switch, (c) add unit perf test for short-chat profiles.
ajay: agree. can someone open the revert PR and the follow-up? mark as rollout-blocker. :warning:
sam: opening revert PR now: https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/4310 (revert 4152)
ci-bot: started job canary/retest after revert PR applied to canary branch.
perf-bot: preliminary after revert: p50=27ms, p95=74ms. still slightly above baseline but within noise.
laura: leaving notes for post-mortem: - quant routing had unintended dequant hotpath exposure - kernel switch toggled batching flag - lack of short-chat perf regression test in CI - missing KV-hit profiling in release gating
maya: thanks all. after follow-up PRs we should add a deopt checklist for any kernel-routing change. also add a lightweight synthetic test (seq_len 8 chat) to perf CI so this doesn't regress silently.
ajay: I'll own the follow-up. assigning ticket PERF-912.
maya: closing loop: revert merged to canary, monitoring dashboards show rollback within 8m, keeping canary paused until follow-ups merged. :lock: 
laura: post-mortem draft coming later today.
maya: :thumbsup:
